newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LE TISSIER SPOILS DALGLISH'S BIG DAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LE TISSIER SPOILS DALGLISH'S BIG DAY.

text.p: An afternoon which seemed about to give Kenny Dalglish a dream start as Newcastle's manager ended in stunning anti-climax for the United faithful on Saturday when Southampton scored twice in the last two minutes to force a 2-2 draw at The Dell.

Newcastle, who appointed Dalglish as manager on Tuesday following Kevin Keegan's departure the previous week, had survived some tremendous Southampton pressure to go into the last few minutes 1-0 ahead thanks to a 14th minute goal from Les Ferdinand.
And they seemed to have got all three points wrapped up when Lee Clark pounced on some indecisive defending to make it 2-0 with only eight minutes to go for his third goal in successive games.
But then with 88 minutes on the clock, all the old frailties that contributed to the stress that led to Keegan resigning, manifested themselves again.

Newcastle keeper Shaka Hislop dropped a cross allowing Neil Maddison to shoot home from close range and then deep into injury time, Matt Le Tissier powered in a 25-metre drive that gave Hislop no chance. There was no time to restart and for the second successive week Newcastle had let slip a two-goal lead and had to settle for a point.
"You just have to hit them when they fall like that," said Le Tissier. "The only thought in my head when I shot was that it was going into the back of the net and luckily it did."
That goal -- and the result -- was an arrow into the heart of Newcastle's title aspirations as leaders Liverpool and second-placed Manchester United both won.

Liverpool just about ended Aston Villa's title hopes with a 3-0 win at Anfield where 18-year-old local discovery Jamie Carragher scored on his full debut, also notable for him being booked 20 seconds after the match began. Stan Collymore got the second, and Robbie Fowler, who scored five goals against Aston Villa last season, added the third. All the goals came in a 13-minute spell in the second half.

Manchester United stretched their unbeaten league run to 11 matches with a 2-0 win at Coventry where the Sky Blues' Gordon Strachan was facing his old club for the first time as manager. Goals from Ryan Giggs (60th) and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer (79th) gave United, who have not lost at Coventry since 1988, all three points and left Coventry perilously close to the relegation zone.
There was plenty of drama at Middlesbrough, who ended a bad week with a welcome 4-2 win over Sheffield Wednesday, who had not lost for 13 matches.

Bryan Robson's men had plummeted to the bottom of the table after winning just one of their last 16 league games. On Tuesday they had three points deducted for pulling out of a match against Blackburn last month without permission and their Italian striker Fabrizio Ravanelli was talking freely about relegation.
But they tore into the visitors from the off, and deservedly took an early lead.
Ravanelli, whose future at the club is the subject of much speculation, put Boro ahead from a 14th minute penalty after Dejan Stefanovic had handled a Mickel Beck cross.

Another Italian, Gianluca Festa, making his debut after his midweek transfer from Inter-Milan, made it 2-0 after 23 minutes, but Wednesday came back with Mark Pembridge's fourth goal in four games six minutes later.

Brazilian Emerson put Middlesbrough 3-1 ahead with another penalty after 72 minutes, and although Pembridge scored again eight minutes later, the Brazilian Juninho made it 4-2 in the last minute. By then though Boro's sad week had taken another twist with Ravanelli sent off for a second bookable offence.
The result left Middlesbrough still at the bottom, two points behind Southampton, and Nottingham Forest, who play Tottenham on Sunday.
There was also drama at Stamford Bridge where Aljosa Asanovic shot Derby into the lead with a 35-metre free kick after 25 minutes.
But the home side fought back with Dennis Wise (36th), Frank LeBouef (44th pen) and debutant substitute Paul Hughes (85th) scoring for Chelsea.
The afternoon which began so well for Derby ended dismally when substitute Christian Dailly picked up Derby's first red-card of the season for a second bookable offence near the end.
